say: Last week, we built this safari website on my laptop. Right now, a client can't see it. In the next few minutes, it'll have a real link you can send on WhatsApp. And it won't cost anything.
And stay to the end. There's one error almost everyone hits after deploying, and the fix takes thirty seconds.

heading: Today
items: Create a free static site on Render
say: Four steps. Push the code to GitHub. Create a free static site on Render. Fix the refresh error. Then set up auto deploy, so every change goes live by itself.

lines: Create a .gitignore for a Vite React project, make the first commit, and tell me the commands to push to a new GitHub repo called kilima-safaris.
say: Render deploys from GitHub, so first, the code goes there. I'll let Claude Code do the boring part. Create a git ignore file, make the first commit, and give me the commands to push to a new repo.
Check that the git ignore includes node modules and the dot env file. Never push your secret keys to GitHub.
Create an empty repo on GitHub, run the two push commands, and refresh. Your code is online.

small: Last week's video is linked at the top
say: If you missed last week's video, where we built this site with A.I., it's linked up here. Subscribe, and you'll get the next step every Thursday.

heading: On render.com
say: Now the free hosting. Go to render dot com and sign up with your GitHub account. Click New, then Static Site, and pick the kilima safaris repo.

heading: The 3 settings that matter
items: Build command: npm install && npm run build
say: Three settings matter. The build command is, npm install, then npm run build. The publish directory is dist, because that's where Vite puts the finished site. And the branch is main.

lines: ==> Running build command 'npm install && npm run build'
say: Click create, and watch the logs. It clones your code, runs the build, and uploads the result. When it says live, open the link.
And there it is. A real address anyone can open. It works. Now, let me break it.
Click tours. Fine. Now refresh the page. Not found. Your site works, until someone refreshes, or shares a link to an inner page. A client will find this in a day.

nodes: Server looks for a file called tours
say: Here's why. The server looks for a file called tours. It doesn't exist. Your React app handles that page, but only when it starts from index dot html.

heading: Redirects and Rewrites
say: The fix. In Render, open redirects and rewrites, and add one rule. Source, slash star. Destination, slash index dot html. Action, rewrite. Save.
Refresh again. Fixed. Every page now works, even from a shared link.

lines: Change the hero headline to: Your Tanzania safari starts here.
Render: new deploy started... live in 58s
say: Best part. Every time you push to GitHub, Render rebuilds the site by itself. I ask Claude Code to change the headline, push, and in about a minute the live site updates. That's how you deliver client changes, without touching a server.

heading: Recap
items: Code on GitHub, keys never pushed
Static site on Render: build, dist, main
say: Quick recap. Code on GitHub, keys never pushed. A static site on Render, with the build command, dist, and main. One rewrite rule for the refresh error. And push to update.
